response: {"title":"Top-three invariant probes","intervention":"Before any full-suite run, identify the three highest-impact invariants affected across module boundaries and test each with one focused probe in descending impact order, using no more than half of the remaining task time for all three probes.","claim":"Compared with no appended instruction, this bounded invariant-probe instruction will increase hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses on multi-module Python tasks.","mechanism":"Explicitly ranking cross-module invariants directs verification toward semantic composition failures that file-local tests overlook, while limiting the probes to half the remaining time preserves completion capacity.","assumptions":["The agent can infer affected invariants from requirements, code, and the diff.","Three invariants capture a useful portion of catastrophic regression risk.","Focused probes can be executed within the stated cap."],"risks":["The inferred invariants may be incomplete or wrong.","The three-item limit can omit a lower-impact but likely failure.","Probe creation can take longer than execution and erode the cap.","The remaining half may be insufficient for repairs after a late failure."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"On matched fixed-deadline tasks, randomly append the instruction or append nothing, holding model, tool access, and hidden-test evaluation constant.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"Treatment improves pass_rate and does not increase the deadline-miss rate; wall_time and turns reveal whether gains require more effort."},"single_shot_ordinal":7}
